You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 63781394c540dd9e666a6b21d70b64dd52bce76e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Axel Lin <axel.lin@ingics.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2015 17:02:58 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] genirq: devres: Fix testing return value of
 request_any_context_irq()

request_any_context_irq() returns a negative value on failure.
It returns either IRQC_IS_HARDIRQ or IRQC_IS_NESTED on success.
So fix testing return value of request_any_context_irq().

Also fixup the return value of devm_request_any_context_irq() to make it
consistent with request_any_context_irq().

Fixes: 0668d3065128 ("genirq: Add devm_request_any_context_irq()")
Signed-off-by: Axel Lin <axel.lin@ingics.com>
Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <sboyd@codeaurora.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/1431334978.17783.4.camel@ingics.com
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
---
 kernel/irq/devres.c | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/kernel/irq/devres.c b/kernel/irq/devres.c
index d5d0f7345c54..74d90a754268 100644
--- a/kernel/irq/devres.c
+++ b/kernel/irq/devres.c
@@ -104,7 +104,7 @@ int devm_request_any_context_irq(struct device *dev, unsigned int irq,
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	rc = request_any_context_irq(irq, handler, irqflags, devname, dev_id);
-	if (rc) {
+	if (rc < 0) {
 		devres_free(dr);
 		return rc;
 	}
@@ -113,7 +113,7 @@ int devm_request_any_context_irq(struct device *dev, unsigned int irq,
 	dr->dev_id = dev_id;
 	devres_add(dev, dr);
 
-	return 0;
+	return rc;
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL(devm_request_any_context_irq);
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by incorrect handling of the return value from the `request_any_context_irq()` function. The original code checked if the return value was non-zero to determine if the request had failed, but this was incorrect because the function returns a negative value on failure. The patch corrects this by checking if the return value is less than zero, ensuring that failure cases are properly identified and handled. Additionally, the return value of `devm_request_any_context_irq()` was also updated to be consistent with the behavior of `request_any_context_irq()`, returning the actual error code on failure instead of always returning zero.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by incorrect handling of the return value from the `request_any_context_irq()` function. The original code checked if the return value was non-zero to determine if the request had failed, but this was incorrect because the function returns a negative value on failure. The patch corrects this by checking if the return value is less than zero, ensuring that failure cases are properly identified and handled. Additionally, the return value of `devm_request_any_context_irq()` was also updated to be consistent with the behavior of `request_any_context_irq()`, returning the actual error code on failure instead of always returning zero.
